summary:
ArtemisOS is a simple-to-use yet advanced lunar landing site navigator with a custom LunaTrek engine built on SPICE, enabling rapid checking of feasible landing sites by choosing custom coordinates.

Other tools that provide such kind of information are built for detailed analysis and are often difficult for non-specialists to access and/or use effectively. ArtemisOS is simple-to-use with its intuitive and easy to understand front end.

Our project is important mainly because it will support mission planners during mission development and also help serve as an educational tool to help students and the general public understand challenges faced in lunar exploration.
details:
ArtemisOS: LunaTrek Engine

ArtemisOS is a desktop-based lunar landing site navigator engineered for high-latitude and polar exploration (-87°S to -90°S) i.e. the Lunar South Pole. It provides mission planners and automated descent systems with deep spatial and temporal analysis tools.

Specifically, it calculates surface elevation and terrain slope hazards via LOLA DEM data, evaluates long-term solar illumination windows, tracks direct Line-of-Sight communication with Earth, and computes critical horizon masking angles (SCritTheta, ECritTheta) to identify optimal, water-ice-adjacent landing windows.

All of it is calculated by its own engine: LunaTrek

How it works

ArtemisOS runs entirely locally via a custom-built simulation and orbital mechanics engine, completely independent of any external web APIs.

· Backend Engine (LunaTrek): Uses NASA SPICE ephemeris kernels (spiceypy) to map accurate time-series vectors for the Sun and Earth relative to any user-selected lunar surface coordinate. It processes high-resolution raster elevation grids (rasterio) to construct 2.5D isometric topography profiles and determine local horizon obstructions.

· Vector Math & Ray-Casting: The Engine transforms raw geospatial raster grids into a 3D Cartesian space, utilizing dynamic azimuth ray-casting, vector dot-product normal projections, and array gradients (np.gradient) to account for lunar curvature and compute true local horizon profiles and surface slopes.

· Frontend & Architecture: Powered by a ReactJS/Vite frontend communicating with a local Python/Flask backend, wrapped into a single, self-contained native window (pywebview / standalone Windows .exe) that bundles all geological datasets and dependency kernels internally.

Benefits of ArtemisOS

· Full Autonomy & Reliability: Operates completely offline without requiring internet connectivity or external API services, making it ideal for secure or field mission-control environments.

· Precision Polar Mapping: Targets treacherous polar regions (like Shackleton Crater and de Gerlache) where traditional global maps fall short.

· Multi-Constraint Optimization: Automatically scores and ranks landing windows based on lighting duration, terrain slope safety, and Earth communication availability.

· Streamlined Distribution: Compiled into a single, portable Windows executable (.exe) that packs all backend logic, frontend assets, and lunar topographical data into one click-and-run package.

Our aim and what we hope to achieve

We aim to provide mission designers, researchers, and space agencies with a rapid, highly accurate decision-support tool for upcoming Artemis missions. By automating the identification of safe, illuminated, and communication-linked landing sites near permanently shadowed regions (PSRs), ArtemisOS helps lower the risks of lunar surface operations and accelerate the search for lunar water-ice resources.

Tech Stack

· Languages: Python, JavaScript, HTML/CSS

· Backend Framework & Libraries: Flask, spiceypy (Orbital Mechanics & SPICE Kernels), rasterio & pyproj (DEM and Geospatial Processing), NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib (for real-time profile rendering)

· Frontend Framework & Tooling: React, Vite, HTML5/CSS3 Canvas

· Packaging & Deployment: PyInstaller (for compiling the standalone Windows .exe bundle)

· Data Sources: NASA LOLA high-resolution lunar South Pole elevation datasets (.tif), SPICE ephemeris kernels (.bsp, .tls, .tpc)
